clue.text: Shrub for a fellow to get out of the earth

parts.note: Jas is the old written abbreviation of James, a man's name standing for any fellow

parts.words: to get out of the earth
parts.note: to mine is to dig ore or coal out of the ground

explanation.surface: A man is told to dig a bush out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: JAS is the traditional abbreviation of the name James.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasmine is a climbing bush with fragrant white or yellow flowers.

clue.text: Bird giving a card a roll up

parts.note: the jack is a court card in a pack of playing cards

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a wad is a roll or bundle, as of banknotes

explanation.surface: A gambler's card produces a bird when rolled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns WAD into DAW beneath JACK.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small grey-naped member of the crow family.

clue.text: The unchaste play with their favourites

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar casually
pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: Promiscuous people amuse themselves with the ones they like best.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpets is an old word for loose women, so it stands for unchaste people.

clue.text: Articles which appear at various times

indicators.note: at various suggests the letters of the next word appear in varied positions

explanation.surface: Goods turn up from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at various' rearranges TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual things or articles, as on a list.

clue.text: Involve a row arising about an expression of gratitude

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other here
arising means getting up, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: a line is a row, as of people or chairs
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in a quarrel over saying thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns LINE into ENIL, and 'about' puts it round TA. TA is everyday British slang for 'thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to bring it along necessarily, to involve it.

clue.text: Resentment when gone astray after failure

indicators.note: after places the rearranged piece behind the word for failure

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters go out of order

explanation.surface: Bitterness sets in when things go wrong after a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges GONE into GEON, which 'after' puts behind DUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offended indignation, as in 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Two-way. preparation for dinner

parts.note: one may change clothes formally before dining, or make the sauce poured over a salad: two ways to get ready for a meal

explanation.walkthrough: The word covers both changing into evening clothes for dinner and the sauce put on food, hence 'two-way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing is both putting on clothes and a sauce for a salad, each a preparation for a meal.

clue.text: People who descend in holding nothing to be a pastime

parts.note: divers go down under water

indicators.note: holding means the word in keeps something inside it

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers going down treat it as a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O inside IN to make ION after DIVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is an entertainment or amusement, something done for fun.

clue.text: The continent with no time for this plant

indicators.note: with no means the time word is taken away from the continent

parts.note: America is a continent
am marks time before noon

explanation.surface: A plant grows on a landmass where the clocks don't matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes AM, morning time, out of AMERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical name of heath and heather.

clue.text: Apparel for a close association

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a bond or association

explanation.surface: Clothing suited to an intimate relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment worn to bed.

clue.text: Prevailing animal is given an income

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog, an animal
rent is income a landlord receives

explanation.surface: A dominant beast is handed some earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means generally accepted or prevalent at present.

clue.text: Most of the people competing are showing their jealousy

indicators.note: most of means one letter is dropped from the word for people

parts.note: men stands for people in general
vying means competing

explanation.surface: Most of the contestants are green with jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops one letter from MEN, leaving EN before VYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Envying is coveting what others have, the act of being jealous of them.

clue.text: Being a household worker, a strange maid converts set

indicators.note: strange suggests the words that follow are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: A peculiar maid turns a set of people to her own beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges MAID CONVERTS SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic servant is a maid, butler or cook employed in a home.

clue.text: Use force on a bird with honour

parts.note: the wren is a small brown bird
CH is the abbreviation of Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: Someone manhandles a decorated bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The CH (Companion of Honour) is a British order awarded for public service.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench is to twist or pull forcibly.

clue.text: Heating apparatus which is potentially over two hundred ton

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, so two of them make two hundred

explanation.surface: A heater could weigh more than a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges OVER, CC and TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A convector is a heater that warms a room by circulating air.

clue.text: Coveted what is half seen and capable of survival

indicators.note: half means only one of the two halves of the word seen is taken

parts.note: viable means able to live or survive

explanation.surface: Something prized is glimpsed and able to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps EN, the back half of SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enviable describes something others would covet.

clue.text: Low fellow enters playwright for the defence

indicators.note: enters means the fellow goes inside the playwright's name

parts.note: J M Barrie wrote Peter Pan
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel bursts in on a dramatist's courtroom defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a defensive barrier blocking a way.

clue.text: The court is risky without the Queen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the risky word goes round the Queen

parts.note: chancy means risky
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Proceedings are hazardous when the monarch is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: CHANCY goes round ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the High Court in England.

clue.text: Drink which is mixed in the basin

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink made up in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges THE BASIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: One who tries to get his own back takes a five to the green possibly

definitions.text: One who tries to get his own back

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: possibly says the word green may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A golfer seeking revenge takes five to reach the green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GREEN into ENGER after A and V.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger takes revenge for a wrong done.

clue.text: Jacket for a king embracing a woman

indicators.note: embracing means the outer letters hold the woman's name between them

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Nora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A coat for a monarch who is hugging a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts NORA between A and K.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket.

clue.text: Creature used in darkest religious rites

indicators.note: used in signals the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An animal is sacrificed in sinister ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points to KESTREL inside 'darKEST RELigious'.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hovers over fields.

clue.text: Conversation which is opposed to the marvellous?

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
fab is slang for fabulous or marvellous

explanation.surface: A chat that is against wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab is an informal chat, short for confabulation.

clue.text: Oriental company in the rear sets free Essex, for example

definitions.note: Essex is a single example of the group, which is plural

indicators.note: in the rear places the releasing word at the back

parts.note: oriental means eastern
unties means sets loose

explanation.surface: An Eastern firm's rear releases an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; the Eastern Counties are the English counties of that region.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is one of the counties in the east of England.

clue.text: Thus they are in France for the geological materials

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
ils is the French for they

explanation.surface: Geological matter is described in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Soils are the earths formed from weathered rock and organic matter.

clue.text: What crews would be if the little ones were included

definitions.text: What crews would be if the little ones were included

parts.words: What crews would be if the little ones were included
parts.note: a rowing eight has a small cox steering besides the oarsmen; count the cox and the crew is one larger

explanation.walkthrough: The 'little ones' are the coxes, traditionally small and light, who steer a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight with its cox numbers one more than eight, so crews would be in groups of that size.

clue.text: The kind of meat a girl set about

indicators.note: about here means turned around, in disorder

explanation.surface: A girl sets about preparing a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges GIRL SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage found in poor-quality meat.

clue.text: Entertainment for noisy cheats?

parts.note: a loud fairground full of rigged stalls, read as amusement for those who play unfairly

explanation.walkthrough: Fairground stalls have a reputation for being rigged, and the place is noisy: the clue suggests a playground for cheats.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair is an outdoor amusement of rides and stalls.

clue.text: Most of the others intercede to produce a fresh colour

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the others word is cut

parts.note: the rest are the others
to pray is to intercede on someone's behalf

explanation.surface: The rest plead for a new paint job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts REST to RES before PRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To respray is to paint a car or surface again in a new colour.

clue.text: Top person almost fit for a biographer

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the top person is cut off

parts.note: the boss is the person in charge
well means fit and healthy

explanation.surface: A leading figure who is nearly healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BOSS to BOS before WELL. James Boswell wrote the Life of Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell is famous for his biography of Samuel Johnson.
